record.paper_title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
record.original_question: Let K be a Keimel-Lawson category, meaning a full subcategory of Top0 satisfying the paper's axioms (K1)-(K4), including containing Sob. Does the K-reflection functor preserve arbitrary products of T0 spaces; equivalently, for every family {X_i}, is (prod_i X_i)^K homeomorphic to prod_i X_i^K?

evidence.quote: Question 7.15. ([49]) Let K be a Keimel-Lawson category. Does the K-reflection functor preserves arbitrary products of T0 spaces?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbf{Top}_0$ denote the category of $T_0$ topological spaces with continuous maps, and let $\mathbf{Sob}$ denote its full subcategory of sober spaces. A full subcategory $\mathbf{K}$ of $\mathbf{Top}_0$ is called a Keimel–Lawson category if it satisfies the following four axioms:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(K1)] $\mathbf{K}$ contains $\mathbf{Sob}$; equivalently, every sober space lies in $\mathbf{K}$.
\item[(K2)] $\mathbf{K}$ is closed under homeomorphisms and under the formation of (topological) products in $\mathbf{Top}_0$.
\item[(K3)] $\mathbf{K}$ is closed under the formation of equalizers in $\mathbf{Top}_0$; equivalently, if $X \in \mathbf{K}$ and $A \subseteq X$ is an equalizer subspace of two continuous maps with codomain in $\mathbf{K}$, then $A \in \mathbf{K}$.
\item[(K4)] For every $X \in \mathbf{K}$, every continuous map $f : Y \to X$ from a $T_0$ space $Y$ admits a unique continuous extension along a suitable canonical embedding so that $\mathbf{K}$ is reflective in $\mathbf{Top}_0$.
\end{itemize}
Under these axioms there exists a reflector $(-)^{\mathbf{K}} : \mathbf{Top}_0 \to \mathbf{K}$, called the $\mathbf{K}$-reflection, left adjoint to the inclusion. 

Question: Does the $\mathbf{K}$-reflection functor preserve arbitrary products of $T_0$ spaces? Equivalently, is it true that for every family $\{X_i\}_{i \in I}$ of $T_0$ spaces the canonical continuous map
\[\Big(\prod_{i \in I} X_i\Big)^{\mathbf{K}} \longrightarrow \prod_{i \in I} X_i^{\mathbf{K}}\]
is a homeomorphism?
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist: for "adequate" Keimel–Lawson categories (which include sober spaces, d-spaces, well-filtered spaces, and the original Keimel–Lawson category), the K-reflection preserves finite products of T0 spaces. The general question of preservation of arbitrary (infinite) products of T0 spaces by the K-reflection of an arbitrary Keimel–Lawson category does not appear to have been fully resolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: The reflectivity of some categories of T0 spaces in domain theory
status_evidence.snippet: If K is adequate, then the K-reflection preserves finite products of T0 spaces; the category of sober spaces, d-spaces, well-filtered spaces and the Keimel–Lawson category are all adequate.
status_evidence.claim: Finite product preservation is established for adequate Keimel–Lawson categories, but arbitrary products are not addressed in the same generality.

status_evidence.title: A direct approach to K-reflections of T0 spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Direct construction of K-reflections for Keimel–Lawson categories.
status_evidence.claim: Construction-level results known, full preservation of arbitrary products remains to be established in general.
